chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Do I perform any of the rituals of Hajj while I am without ablution?' He said, 'Yes, except for Tawaf around the House, for indeed it contains prayer.'

And there is no harm if a person rides between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, but walking is superior. If he rides, let him make his mount move quickly during the Mas'a. Likewise, there is no harm if he rests between them by sitting or in a similar manner. Narrated.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Safa (one of the hills in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: Does one need wudu for Tawaf and Sa'i during Hajj?
ai.summary: Reported by Safwan ibn Yahya and transmitted through the chain of Ibn Abi Umayr, this hadith clarifies that while most Hajj rituals do not strictly require wudu, Tawaf is uniquely treated as a prayer (salah) necessitating ritual purity. It further elaborates on the jurisprudence of Sa'i, affirming that while walking is superior (afdhal), riding is permissible provided the pilgrim accelerates during the designated 'masa' areas, reflecting the practical flexibility emphasized in Shia fiqh.
